stories.headline: Humanity's Last Exam published in Nature: frontier AI scores only 40-50% on expert test

key_facts.fact: Nearly 1,000 experts from over 50 countries created a 2,500-question benchmark spanning 100+ subjects including mathematics, humanities, natural sciences, and ancient languages.
key_facts.excerpt: Nearly 1,000 experts from more than 50 countries collaborated to build a new assessment called Humanity's Last Exam, or HLE, a 2,500-question test covering more than 100 subjects.

key_facts.fact: GPT-4o scored 2.7%, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 4.1%, OpenAI's o1 about 8%, while Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus 4.6 reached 40-50% accuracy — still far below expert human performance.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-4o scored 2.7%, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 4.1%, and OpenAI's o1 model reached about 8% accuracy. More recent systems, such as Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus 4.6, improved to around 40-50% accuracy.

key_facts.fact: Questions were deliberately designed so any question correctly answered by current AI models at the time was removed, ensuring the exam measures genuine capability gaps.
key_facts.excerpt: Every question was tested against leading AI models. Any question correctly answered by current AI was removed.

key_facts.fact: The study was published in Nature and led by Texas A&M's Dr. Tung Nguyen, who stated: 'intelligence isn't just about pattern recognition — it's about depth, context and specialized expertise.'
key_facts.excerpt: Dr. Nguyen stated: 'When AI systems start performing extremely well on human benchmarks, it's tempting to think they're approaching human-level understanding. But HLE reminds us that intelligence isn't just about pattern recognition — it's about depth, context and specialized expertise.'

key_facts.fact: The benchmark is publicly available at lastexam.ai and is published in Nature (2026; 649(8099): 1139) as a permanent measurement tool for tracking AI progress against the expert human frontier.
key_facts.excerpt: To inform research and policymaking upon a clear understanding of model capabilities, we publicly release HLE at https://lastexam.ai.

stories.headline: Trump launches trade probes against dozens of countries to replace $1.6T in tariff revenue

key_facts.fact: The Supreme Court struck down Trump's emergency tariffs on February 20, 2026, eliminating approximately $1.6 trillion in expected tariff revenue over the next decade according to the CBO.
key_facts.excerpt: The Trump administration this week stepped up its ambitious effort to replace about $1.6 trillion in lost tariff revenue that was eliminated by the Supreme Court's decision to strike down a range of the president's import taxes.

key_facts.fact: Trump launched unfair trade practice investigations into dozens of countries including allies like Canada, Mexico, the UK, and the EU, covering excess industrial capacity and forced labor compliance.
key_facts.excerpt: The Trump administration has launched unfair trade practices investigations into dozens of countries. The probes will look into everything from excess industrial capacity to whether other countries are doing enough to combat forced labor.

key_facts.fact: Trump now relies on Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act, which requires longer processes including public hearings and industry comment. A factory capacity investigation hearing is set for May 5, and a forced labor hearing for April 28.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump is now relying on Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act, which requires longer, more complex processes including consultations with targeted countries, public hearings, and industry commentary.

key_facts.fact: A temporary 10% tariff on all imports was imposed under separate legal authority for 150 days, with the potential to raise it to 15%.

stories.headline: Brent crude closes at $103 as IEA calls Hormuz crisis 'largest oil disruption in history'

key_facts.fact: Brent crude rose 2.67% to close at $103.14/bbl on March 13, the highest in over three years. US WTI crude settled at $98.71/bbl, up 3.11%.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent futures rose 2.67%, or $2.68, to close at $103.14 per barrel. U.S. crude oil gained 3.11%, or $2.98, to settle at $98.71 per barrel.

key_facts.fact: The IEA characterized the Hormuz crisis as 'the largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market' and agreed to release a record 400 million barrels from strategic stockpiles, with the US contributing 172 million barrels.
key_facts.excerpt: The war in the Middle East is creating the largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market.

key_facts.fact: The US issued a second 30-day sanctions waiver for Russian oil loaded before March 12, broader than the initial India-only directive. Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev said it would free up an estimated 100 million barrels.
key_facts.excerpt: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced on Thursday the temporary waiver of sanctions on Russian oil and petroleum products for a period of 30 days. Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev said the move would free up for buyers an estimated 100 million bbl of Russian oil.

key_facts.fact: Trump is considering suspending the Jones Act to allow non-American tankers to transport energy between domestic ports, as the Hormuz blockade has idled hundreds of vessels and sent charter rates soaring.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump said Friday he was considering suspending the Jones Act to allow non-American tankers to transport energy and agricultural products between local ports amid a squeeze in vessel availability.

key_facts.fact: Gas prices have risen 65 cents per gallon since the war began, with the national average climbing rapidly.
key_facts.excerpt: Americans acutely feeling the pain at the pump, the national price for a gallon of gas is up 65 cents just since the war with Iran began.

stories.headline: Qatar helium shutdown from Iranian drone strikes puts semiconductor supply chain on two-week clock

key_facts.fact: QatarEnergy's Ras Laffan facility, responsible for nearly a third of global helium supply, has been offline since March 2 following Iranian drone strikes. QatarEnergy declared force majeure on March 4.
key_facts.excerpt: QatarEnergy declared force majeure on existing contracts on March 4, freeing it from supply obligations to customers.

key_facts.fact: Helium consultant Phil Kornbluth warned that if the outage extends beyond two weeks, distributors would be forced to relocate cryogenic equipment and revalidate supplier relationships — a process stretching months.
key_facts.excerpt: Helium consultant Phil Kornbluth, speaking at a Gasworld webinar on March 4, said that if the outage extends beyond roughly two weeks, industrial gas distributors could be forced to relocate cryogenic equipment and revalidate supplier relationships.

key_facts.fact: South Korea sourced 64.7% of its helium from Qatar in 2025 and is among the most exposed countries. Seoul's Ministry of Trade opened a review of 14 critical supply items.
key_facts.excerpt: South Korea is among the most exposed countries, which, according to the Korea International Trade Association, imported 64.7% of its helium from Qatar in 2025.

key_facts.fact: Helium is essential for cooling silicon wafers during chip fabrication and has no effective substitute. The halted Qatari output removed an estimated 5 million cubic meters of monthly helium from the global market.
key_facts.excerpt: Helium prices surged after Qatar halted liquefied natural gas production this week, removing an estimated 5 million cubic meters of monthly helium output from the global market.

stories.headline: YolTech gets FDA clearance for in vivo gene-editing therapy YOLT-202 targeting Alpha-1 deficiency

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved YolTech Therapeutics' IND application for YOLT-202, an in vivo adenine base-editing therapy that corrects the PiZ mutation to PiM in Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency (AATD), enabling a Phase 2/3 clinical trial.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the Investigational New Drug (IND) application for YOLT-202, the company's investigational in vivo base-editing therapy for the treatment of Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency (AATD).

key_facts.fact: In a first-in-human trial with two patients, YOLT-202 showed rapid dose-dependent AAT level increases by Week 1, with the 45mg dose achieving normal range (>20 μM) with >95% corrected M-AAT protein.
key_facts.excerpt: The 45 mg dose group achieved normal range (>20 μM) with >95% corrected M-AAT protein. The newly produced proteins were both structurally corrected and functional.

key_facts.fact: CEO Yuxuan Wu characterized YOLT-202 as a potential 'one and done' therapy. The drug previously received Orphan Drug Designation from the FDA.
key_facts.excerpt: CEO Yuxuan Wu characterized it as potential 'one and done' therapy. YOLT-202 previously received Orphan Drug Designation from the FDA.

key_facts.fact: The Phase 2/3 study will be an open-label, single-dose multiregional clinical trial across US and international sites for adult patients with AATD.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA approval enables the initiation of an open-label, single-dose expansion Phase 2/3 clinical study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of YOLT-202 in adult patients with Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency.
